unit: R-W18 re-review round 1 (W1-8b/W1-8c/W1-8d plus the census minor): retro/w1-8-adapter-drop, wip e1d7be86 above base 1c6f6796, with the fixer's uncommitted edits on top. Worktree C:/Users/SynAckITPC/Documents/AI/sc-r-w18
tests_that_prove_nothing: Mutant A01 SURVIVED (47/47 green). In _safe_exc_url, `if "?" in rest[:at] or "#" in rest[:at]` was changed to `if "?" in rest[:at]`, so the check no longer looks for '#'. Nothing pins the case where an '@' sits in a URL fragment. Under the mutant, 'https://h.example/cb#access_token=S5&e=a@b.com&k=S9' would come out as 'https://b.com&k=S9' and leak S9. I probed the real code on that input and it gives 'https://[redacted] y', so the code is correct and only the pin is missing. test_w18d_safe_exc_fixer_shapes covers '#' only inside a password, and that case is safe even without the check, because userinfo is cut at the last '@'.

Mutant A04 SURVIVED. `_wave_finished = [0]` was moved above the wave loop, so the counter is shared by both waves. No test runs a render-wave TIMEOUT after a curl wave, so the per-wave reset is unpinned. Under the mutant, pending would read len(render) - (curl_finished + render_finished) and could go negative. I probed the real code through _get_price (curl wave: 3 instant misses; render wave: 1 miss and 1 hang; budget 1.5 s) and it gives 'wave=curl completed=3 failed=0 cancelled=0' then 'wave=render TIMEOUT pending=1', so the code is correct.

Mutants B01 and B02 SURVIVED. The walrus captures the consume bound in the jsonapi INLINE branch (`timeout=(_ja_bound := _consume_bound()),`) and in the _new_adapter_specs INLINE branch (`timeout=(_na_bound := _consume_bound()),`). Removing either one would make those lines log 'CONSUME-BOUND after 0.00s'. These are the same shape as the adversary's N08. The fixer added a pin for the sitemap inline branch only: test_w18c_consume_bound_inline_sitemap_branch_names_its_bound. The prefetch-branch twins B03 (_na) and B04 (sitemap) were KILLED.

Mutant A15 SURVIVED. The sitemap CONSUME-BOUND line was changed to recompute `_consume_bound()` when it logs, instead of printing the captured `_sm_bound`. The consume-bound tests patch _pre_reserve_remaining to a constant 0.3, so recomputing gives the same number and no test can tell whether the bound was captured at the wait. In production the deadline has moved by the time the line is logged, so a recomputed value would understate the bound the code actually waited under.

Mutant A16 SURVIVED. The per-wave summary elapsed was changed to fan_out's own `elapsed_seconds` instead of the measured `time.monotonic() - _wave_t0`. test_w18b_wave_summary_elapsed_is_measured (the fixer's N11 pin) accepts anything in [0.25, 5.0). Its stub fan_out returns the canned _winner elapsed of 0.42, which falls inside that window, so the pin does not prove the value is measured at the call site. The two values are nearly equal in production.

Mutant A07 SURVIVED. In _timeout_none, the wrap-vs-adapter-raised margin `timeout - 0.05` was changed to `timeout - 0.12`. The N01 pin (a raise at 0.85 s of a 1.0 s wrap) only rules out margins of about 0.15 or more, so the ruled 0.05 is pinned loosely. Mutant A06 (SLOW-MISS keyed on `not result` instead of `result is None`) also survived; it is near-equivalent, because the wrapped adapters return Optional[dict].
summary:
SOUND. All four defects from the previous adversary round are closed or correctly disclosed, and I found no blocking or major defect. The fix only adds logging, and every return value I drove through the real functions is unchanged. The surviving mutants in tests_that_prove_nothing are unpinned minor branches; the real code behaves correctly on each of them.

**Start state**
- HEAD is e1d7be86 above 1c6f6796. `git status --short` showed exactly the fixer's three uncommitted edits (M on scs, the census file and test_retro_w1_8.py), and `git diff HEAD` showed only them, as the re-review brief says.
- sha256 of each diff file at start, equal to the fixer's reported final shas:
  - app/services/structured_comparison_service.py: ddbf92ee103071b929c9cafd029fe55a3777cbc6374895c680ecae8e4895b50d
  - tests/test_retro_w1_8.py: 0ff7a0817cd974e320bdf7572bd0a3fc1431a4635d4f08560828f7e4ccb3a6c4
  - tests/test_adapter_drop_visibility.py: ca9f4b6d63ef609b5859012ada7e1b533d2c5675b7aec40c16aa8022fb75d134
- The brief's "33 passed / b2b9bf06" figures describe the pre-fix wip. The current 47 and ddbf92ee match the fix report exactly, so there is no mutant on disk.

**Unit files:** 47 passed on the pinned venv with a process-wide non-loopback netguard plugin (a copy of rw18adv_netguard). The netlog was never created, meaning 0 network attempts.

**Diff review**
- The scs changes are 67 added and 10 removed lines. The file is uniformly CRLF on disk (8770 of 8770 lines) and there is no whole-file diff.
- ruff (E9, F63, F7, F82) and py_compile are clean on all three files.
- New statements:
  - three FETCH-FAIL INFO lines, each inside an existing None-returning branch, with the returns untouched;
  - the `_count_finished` wrapper at the fan_out call site;
  - `_safe_exc` now matches any `<scheme>://` (scheme length bounded) and cuts userinfo at the last '@', redacting the token when a '?' or '#' comes before that '@';
  - the pending count, now len - finished.
- I read fan_out_price_lookup (price_service:16304): it only ever calls `s(product)` and never inspects scrapers, so the wrapper is transparent to it.

**Return identity through the real fan_out (unwrapped vs wrapped)**
I compared best, alternates, failed_count and cancelled_count on six shapes: hit rank 90, hits rank 50, raise, late raise, None, hang, and a scraper that swallows the cancel. All six were identical.

**Unhappy paths probed through the real code**
- Two waves (curl completes, render times out): pending=1, correct.
- Firecrawl through the real service with a 200 carrying invalid JSON: the service maps it to (None, 0), so it logs `FETCH-FAIL status=0`. pr_text's "0 means transport timeout or error" covers this.
- `_safe_exc` edge cases:
  - Handled correctly: upper-case scheme, ws://, percent-encoded userinfo, CRLF between two credentialed URLs, and a quoted repr with a trailing '@'.
  - Still unscrubbed:
    - Scheme-less `user:pw@proxy:8080` is outside the ruled http(s) scope. The honest-limits list names bare api_key and percent-encoding but not this shape.
    - A password with an unencoded space, or a URL whose userinfo starts after U+00A0, is not a valid URL.
    - No real adapter or exception path was shown to produce any of these.
- Defect 3 numbers verified: unbxd_service.py:58 and noon_service.py:102 both clamp with adapter_timeout(8.0), below the 8.5 s threshold. pr_text is now correct about this.

**Mutation checks**
All runs used scratch copies (rw18_adv2/mutroot and proberoot), byte snapshots and sha256-verified restores, never git. An unmutated control passed each time.
- The fixer's full 66-entry list re-run: 60 KILLED, 0 SURVIVED, and the same 6 BAD-ANCHOR entries the fixer re-expressed. The previously surviving N01, N02, N03, N05, N06, N08 and N11 are now KILLED, as are R-N04, R-N07, R-M09, R-M10, R-M14 and F01-F17 (F15 by the pytest-timeout).
- 25 new mutants (A01-A22, then B01-B04): 17 KILLED, 8 SURVIVED (A01, A04, A06, A07, A15, A16, B01, B02). All eight are listed in tests_that_prove_nothing.

**Comm gate at HEAD**
- The recorded 152-file set with the pinned flags and the netguard plugin: 2 failed, 3963 passed, 2 skipped, 29 deselected, 16 warnings, in 303 s.
- The failed set is identical to the recorded base (test_page_scraping.py::TestFetchPagePriceJsonLD::test_jsonld_nested_offers_picks_lowest and ::TestFetchPagePriceOpenGraph::test_og_meta_extraction), and branch-only-NEW is empty. The netlog is absent, meaning 0 attempts.
- I reused the recorded base and created no scratch worktree; `git worktree list` shows no rw18 entry.

**For the orchestrator**
- The fixer's new `FETCH-FAIL` token (`fanout:curl:<d>: FETCH-FAIL no-html` and `fanout:<firecrawl|scrapedo>:<d>: FETCH-FAIL status=<n>`) is outside ruling 3's fixed token set. It needs orchestrator or Fable confirmation, as the fixer itself says. It is logging-only and it is what makes ruling 4's production-signal claim true.
- INFO volume is still unmeasured.

**End state**
- `git status --short` shows the same three M files, and `git diff HEAD --stat` is unchanged. The three shas are identical to the start, so nothing in the worktree was modified; the only untracked or ignored items are `.env`, `.qa-retro/` and `__pycache__`.
- Process disclosure: I ran one `find ... -name __pycache__ -exec rm -r` inside my own scratch copy (scratchpad/rw18_adv2/mutroot) right after copying. It touched no worktree and no shared directory, but it is a recursive delete, which the rules forbid.
